Subject: Atlas Health — Regional capacity & burst questions for Dedicated pool

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for last week's demo. We want to lock in a Dedicated GPU pool and need to confirm a few things before procurement proceeds:

- Primary regions: We plan to serve US-west users first, with EU as a phased second. Can Redwood guarantee regional anchoring and a documented fallback plan if west capacity is constrained?
- Autoscale/burst behavior: What triggers burst vs. warm standby? We expect predictable latency under 95th percentile at 300 qps sustained and occasional spikes to 1,200 qps.
- Networking: Our NetOps (cc'd) needs L4/L7 requirements and whether VPC peering or Direct Connect equivalents are required for low egress latency.
- Security/compliance hygiene: We will request SOC2 evidence and an activation MOP prior to signing the SOW.

I've attached a short intake doc (Atlas_Onboarding_Qs.docx) with traffic shapes and compliance questions. Can we get a consolidated plan and a single point of contact on your side to coordinate NetOps and procurement?

Best,
Samira Khan
Chief Product Officer, Atlas Health

Hi Samira — great to hear from you and thanks for the intake doc. I'll be your engagement lead for the Dedicated activation. Quick outline below; we'll expand into a formal MOP and SOW once we align on region & burst needs.

Summary (high level):
- Regions: We can provision primary capacity in us-west-2. EU staging is available as a separate reserved pool and can be configured as a fallback region. We'll document failover order and expected DNS/edge behavior.
- Autoscale vs. Burst: Redwood supports two mechanisms: autoscale (gradual GPU allocation based on target concurrency and SLOs) and burst (short-term warm capacity held for immediate spikes). For your numbers (300 qps sustained, 1,200 qps spikes) my preliminary recommendation is: sustained baseline via a reserved multipool sized for 400 qps, autoscale headroom to ~700 qps, plus a burst bucket that can be invoked for 30–120s to handle the 1,200 qps peaks.
- NetOps handoff: Rajiv, can your team share preferred topology (VPC peering vs. private link/direct connect), ASN ranges, and firewall egress allowances? We will provide a one-page network checklist and a sample iptables/CNAT map.
- Compliance: We'll attach SOC2 summary and an activation MOP v1 for review.

Next steps:
1) I'll circulate the draft MOP + network checklist by EOD Tuesday.
2) Marcus will scope burst sizing simulations; Monica will coordinate the SOW & procurement items.
3) Rajiv — once we have your network matrix, we'll slot a NetOps call with our infra team.

Cc'ing Monica and Marcus to pick up action items.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Sales — Dedicated, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 16 Sep 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Atlas Health — Regional capacity & burst questions for Dedicated pool

Rafael / team — adding technical detail for sizing and ops: 

- Sizing assumptions: 300 qps baseline translates to ~60 concurrent tokens/streams for the model family Atlas indicated; that maps to 4x A100-equivalent GPUs for baseline load (conservative). Autoscale policy should use a CPU and GPU utilization signal plus request latency to decide scale-up.
- Burst bucket: recommend 8 additional GPUs kept warm in us-west with cold-start <8s. Burst should be invoked automatically by a policy (latency breach OR QPS > 650 for >15s) and should decay back after 90s of low activity.
- Cost-control: enable conservative token-caching on common prefixes (we'll provide a cache-key manifest) and rate-limited fallback to a lower-capacity variant in EU if costs spike.

I'll prepare a short simulation plan (load profile + sequence) and a runbook for burst invocation thresholds. Rafael — happy to join the NetOps call.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Rajiv Mehta <rajiv.mehta@netops.atlashealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Sep 2025 07:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Atlas Health — Regional capacity & burst questions for Dedicated pool

Thanks, Rafael and Marcus. A few NetOps notes: 
- Preferred topology: we prefer AWS Direct Connect to a customer VPC for production (low jitter), with VPC peering to secondary regions. If Direct Connect is not ready at cutover, a private link + encrypted transit is acceptable.
- IP ranges: I'll send CIDR blocks this afternoon. We will require a list of egress FQDNs and port ranges for health checks and telemetry (UDP/TCP).
- MTU and path MTU: ensure jumbo frames are negotiable; we saw issues in earlier pilots when MTU mismatch occurred.

I'll review the redwood-mop-v1 and the network checklist. Can we set a NetOps tech call on Friday at 10:00 PT?

Rgds,
Rajiv Mehta
Sr. Network Engineer, Atlas Health
